analysis:
No concrete regression found. The PR adds a GUI self-update channel: release-desktop.yml embeds a fixed generic https feed (FEED_URL at line 35, passed at line 129). Release builds now refuse to build without a feed (electron-builder.ts:30-31). The DMG is restamped after signing and stapling (workflow 160-161). The verify step greps app-update.yml for the feed URL and runs update-feed.mjs `check` on every feed entry's sha512 and size (workflow 189-192). The feed is published as a mutable prerelease: the zip, blockmap and DMG are uploaded first, then latest-mac.yml last, with --clobber (workflow 230-246).

This is new supply-chain attack surface that the threat model does not describe: the desktop app's update path, with GitHub release write access (contents: write on desktop-v* tags) as the trust anchor. It is adjacent to T-013 and T-034 but not a listed threat; I recommend a threat-model note. The integrity chain is the feed sha512 plus macOS code-signature validation by the updater. Neither is a control this PR introduces, and the updater runtime code is not in the diff. Whether electron-updater/Squirrel.Mac enforces the Developer ID designated requirement, and that downgrades stay disabled, are unverified contracts. The src/main/updateFeed.ts https enforcement (referenced by tests) and the main-process update code were not supplied.

Minor, availability only: non-atomic --clobber uploads can briefly make a fetched feed mismatch the zip (the updater would fail sha512 and retry). The Publish-feed step failing after the release is created blocks a re-run because the 'release already exists' guard fires (workflow 62-65).

The update-feed.mjs YAML handling is regex-based over build-controlled electron-builder output, with no untrusted input. The GUI update does not touch the provider runtime, App Attest qualification (A-016, A-017) or coordinator keys. The desktop bundle is separate from the CLI that the install script downloads.
